chunks: Saad from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lu'lu'i from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal from Abu al-Mi'za Humayd ibn al-Muthanna from Imran from Muhammad ibn Ali: that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

about the traveling man when he joins the prayer with the residents, he said: 'Let him pray his prayer, then give the salutation, and let him make the last two [rak'ahs] a prostration of remembrance (suhbah).'

key_terms.سُبْحَةً: A prostration of remembrance/brevity (a specific short form of prayer)
key_terms.يُسَلِّمُ: To give the salutation (ending the prayer)

ai.seo_question: How should a traveler shorten their prayer if they join the resident's congregational prayer late?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* addresses the specific fiqh of a traveler (musafir) who joins the resident (muqim) congregation after having already performed his own short prayer, a scenario known as *salat al-musafir ma'a al-muqim*. The ruling instructs him to complete the prayer by offering the final salutation and treating the remaining two rak'ahs as *suhbah* (a brief, non-obligatory prostration or remembrance), thereby validating his participation in the four-rak'ah congregational prayer without invalidating his prior short prayer. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the flexibility of prayer shortening (*qasr*) and the validity of joining congregations even when one's individual prayer status differs from the congregation's.
